body.title: Exponential-growth conjecture for Möbius values of the permutations $\kappa_n$
body.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $\kappa_n\in {\mathcal S}_{4n}$ be the permutation

$$
\kappa_n=n+1,n+3,\dots,3n-1,1,3n+1,2,3n+2,\dots,n,4n,n+2,n+4,\dots,3n.
$$

It is $321$-free and can be split into four quadrants, each an increasing subsequence of length $n$. **Exponential-growth conjecture.** The absolute value of its Möbius function satisfies

$$
|\mu(1,\kappa_n)|=\exp(\Theta(n)).
$$

Here “exponential in $n$” is recorded as exponential growth; the paper presents this as a conjecture motivated by computational experiments, and no resolution is supplied.
body.review_depth: Literal kappa_n, primary §4 Conjecture 4.1, comparison with pi_n and chain-count upper bounds read.
body.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: more.py mobius computes exact principal Mobius values by all distinct standardized subpatterns for n=1..4: -1,-27,-117,-509. The largest case caches 5165 patterns. These finite data cannot decide exp(Theta(n)).
body.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Need a recurrence or sign-controlled embedding cancellation for all n; finite nonzero values do not prove exponential growth. A thesis lead with values through kappa_7 was found but its body was not fetched/read.

body.title: Regularity conjecture for even associated lattices
body.statement: Let $a>2$ be even and let $b$ be sufficiently large. Consider an Ulam set with generators $v_1$ and $v_2$ whose associated lattice is generated by $(-a,b)$. **Regularity conjecture.** The Ulam set contains finitely many elements of the form $2xv_1+yv_2$ and is therefore regular. The claim is based on computations and is presented as unresolved in the source.
body.review_depth: Primary associated-lattice definitions, Corollary 4.3 proof, Conjecture 4.4 and Theorem 4.5 scope read. a=2 theorem is outside the reserved a>2 conjecture.
body.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: more.py ulam scans all candidate integers through 100000 for a in {4,6,8,10,12}, b in {101,103,107,109,127,151,199,251,503}, retaining gcd(a,b)=1 only. Here v1=b, v2=a realizes lattice (-a,b); b is odd so generator-v1 parity is integer parity. Per-case total and last even element logged. This omits torsion lattice cases.
body.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Finite apparent termination of even terms cannot prove eventual regularity. Need uniform no-new-even mechanism for sufficiently large b or an infinite exceptional family; no finite sweep can negate the unspecified threshold.

body.title: The run-structure conjecture for words of minimal subword entropy
body.statement:
For $k \geq 2$, let $w$ be a binary word of length $n \geq 1$ achieving the minimal subword entropy $\min S_{\mathrm{sw}}^{(k)}(n)$. A **run** is a maximal consecutive block of equal letters. **Run-structure conjecture.** Except for finitely many values of $n$, the longest run in $w$ has length $3$, and the average run length converges as $n \to +\infty$.

The claim is motivated by computations showing that minimizers mostly contain runs of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$, while long runs appear to increase subword entropy. Its status is open.

body.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Exact integer enumeration of binary words of lengths1..14, first letter0 with partial reversal pruning. Counts all subwords by prefix extension DP, minimizes maxocc, records every retained minimizer run statistic. Largest run3 at n=13,14; ties persist there. Does not extend source 40.

body.title: The uniqueness conjecture for most frequent subwords of minimal binary words
body.statement:
Let $w$ be a binary word of length $n$ achieving the minimal subword entropy. **Uniqueness conjecture.** There are only finitely many values of $n$ for which such a word $w$ has several most frequent subwords.

The conjecture concerns the apparent eventual uniqueness of the most frequent subword among entropy-minimizing binary words. It is supported by the paper's finite computations but remains open.

body.title: Local short-generator conjecture for expanders of ${\rm PSL}_2({\mathbb F}_p)$
body.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $\Sigma_p$ satisfy

$$
\langle \Sigma_p\rangle={\rm PSL}_2({\mathbb F}_p).
$$

**Local short-generator conjecture.** There is a constant $C$, independent of $p$, such that the ball of radius $C$ in the generating set $\Sigma_p$ contains two elements $g,h$ with

$$
\operatorname{girth}\bigl(\mathcal{G}({\rm PSL}_2({\mathbb F}_p),\{g,h\})\bigr)\geq \frac{1}{C}\log p.
$$

Combined with the cited expansion result, this would imply that Cayley graphs of ${\rm SL}_2({\mathbb F}_p)$ are expanders for every choice of generators. The paper provides no resolution.
body.reason: All generating sets and all primes with absolute radius C. Random-generator high-girth theorem does not ensure such a pair inside every constant-radius ball. The raw solved reference concerns a neighboring diophantine theorem.
body.missing_lemma_or_scope_gap: Uniform local high-girth extraction under arbitrary generators; no concrete full proof.

body.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a commutative group, and let an Ulam set in $G$ be generated from two initial generators using unique sums of two earlier distinct elements. **Two-generator infinitude conjecture.** Every Ulam set in a commutative group with two generators is infinite. Finite examples are known with more than two generators, while the source reports no finite two-generator example and leaves this claim unresolved.

body.title: The short most frequent subword conjecture
body.literal_statement:
Let $w$ be a word of length at least $2$. A subword is **most frequent** if it maximizes the number of occurrences in $w$. **Short-subword conjecture.** At least one most frequent subword of $w$ has length at most

$$
\left\lceil \frac{|w|}{2} \right\rceil.
$$

The claim is motivated by lower bounds on maximum subword occurrence counts and by the intuition that sufficiently long subwords cannot be optimal. It is presented as open.
body.source_name: Wenjie Fang, “Maximal number of subword occurrences in a word”, arXiv:2406.02971 (2025).

body.title: The layered-permutation conjecture for maximal Newton-polytope support
body.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $\theta_w$ denote the number of supports of the Schubert polynomial $\mathfrak{S}_w(x)$, equivalently the number of lattice points in its Newton polytope, and define

$$
\beta_n=\max\{\theta_w\colon w\in S_n\}.
$$

A **layered permutation** is a concatenation of decreasing blocks on consecutive intervals. **Layered-maximizer conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$, the permutations in $S_n$ attaining the maximum value $\beta_n$ are layered permutations. This is equivalent to saying that the permutations whose Newton polytopes have the largest number of lattice points are layered permutations; the source reports verification for $n$ up to $9$.
body.investigation: Source Conjecture 5.2 exact support-cardinality maximizers, not principal specialization alpha_n (Conjecture 5.1). Source lists all maximizers through n=9. A larger nonlayered support requires exact polynomial/monomial semantics and comparison with EVERY layered permutation; no such witness obtained.

body.title: Gao's positivity conjecture for permutation-pattern coefficients
body.statement:
For $w\in S_n$, write

$$
\nu_w=1+\sum_{u\in S_m\atop m\leq n}c_u\,p_u(w),
$$

where $p_u(w)$ counts occurrences of the pattern $u$ in $w$, and define the coefficients recursively by

$$
c_u=\nu_u-1-\sum_{\sigma\in S_\ell\atop \ell<m}c_\sigma\,p_\sigma(u).
$$

Here $u$ ranges over permutations and $c_u$ has the stability property $c_u=0$ when the final entry of $u$ is its maximum. **Gao's positivity conjecture.** For any permutation $u$, $c_u\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. The source records proofs for several pattern-avoidance classes, but not the general assertion.
body.investigation: Source Conjecture 5.6 on c_u for principal specializations nu_u. Source 5.7 concerns different d_u for support counts. d_u>c_u at 13452786 is not a negative c_u and does not refute this claim. Need arbitrary pattern coefficient positivity or exact negative witness.

body.title: The higher-genus dual conjecture for Laplacian quadratic forms
body.literal:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be connected graphs of the same genus $g$, and let $\Sigma_g$ be the genus-$g$ surface. Suppose that $G_1$ and $G_2$ have embeddings into $\Sigma_g$ such that their corresponding dual graphs are isomorphic as multigraphs.

**Higher-genus dual conjecture.** The quadratic forms over $\mathbb{Z}$ represented by the combinatorial Laplacians of $G_1$ and $G_2$ are equivalent.

This extends the proposed planar statement to embeddings in minimal-genus surfaces. The source presents it as an extension of the planar conjecture and gives no evidence of a resolution.
